BeforeSideTurnStart.maps_to: before_side_turn_start (red_mask.py:19-24), dispatched by HookSystem.before_side_turn_start (hooks.py:653-668) -- the FIRST hook of the player's turn, matching CombatManager.cs:458
BeforeSideTurnStart.rationale: STALE 2026-07-30: both halves this entry's 2026-07-28 narrowing left open are now closed, and the record was never regenerated after either fix landed. (1) THE SLOT: red_mask.py:19 is `def before_side_turn_start(self, player)`, not `on_player_turn_started` -- this record's own `maps_to` field was already out of date with the code it describes. hooks.py:653-668 documents the slot as 'the FIRST hook of a side's turn ... before the enemies' next-move roll ... before the block clear ... Bag of Marbles, Red Mask, Kunai, Shuriken, Orichalcum ... live here', matching CombatManager.cs:458 exactly (turn_structure step 9). EXECUTED (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/relic-6-checks.py::probe_red_mask_slot_and_hittable`): a spy relic registered alongside Red Mask sees `before_side_turn_start` fire before `on_energy_reset` and `on_player_turn_start`, and turn-1 Weak lands on both enemies of a real encounter. (2) THE ENEMY SET: `relics/base.py` now has both `living_enemies()` and a distinct `hittable_enemies()` (base.py:440-451), and red_mask.py:23 still iterates `living_enemies()` rather than the hittable-only set C#'s `HittableEnemies` would give -- but `PowerCmd.apply` was separately fixed to carry a `can_receive_powers` backstop (cmds.py:540, 590, citing 'CanReceivePowers says no to (PowerCmd.cs:73-76). Round 6 wired the ShouldAllowHitting half') that no-ops the actual power application to any creature `should_allow_hitting` rejects, regardless of which list a caller iterates. EXECUTED: a `PowerCmd.apply(WeakPower)` call against a target with `should_allow_hitting` forced False leaves that target's Weak power `None` -- the same observable C#'s `HittableEnemies` filter produces, reached by a different route. Both guards (G1, G2) are matched below.

ExtraHoverTips.rationale: RelicModel.Flash() / base.Status = RelicStatus.* / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / the N*Vfx nodes are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter and hover text. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.

guards.what: G1 (DORMANT): the sim binds C#'s BeforeSideTurnStart to on_player_turn_started -- turn_structure step 23, where the C# hook is step 9
guards.rationale: CLOSED, RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30: red_mask.py no longer binds to on_player_turn_started at all. The sim grew a dedicated `before_side_turn_start` dispatcher (hooks.py:653-668, 'the FIRST hook of a side's turn ... Bag of Marbles, Red Mask, Kunai, Shuriken, Orichalcum ... live here'), and red_mask.py:19 is `def before_side_turn_start(self, player)` -- the same slot CombatManager.cs:458 fires Hook.BeforeSideTurnStart from (turn_structure step 9), not the step-23/on_player_turn_started slot this guard was written against. EXECUTED (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/relic-6-checks.py::probe_red_mask_slot_and_hittable`): a spy relic sharing the combat sees `before_side_turn_start` fire first, ahead of `on_energy_reset` and `on_player_turn_start`, and both enemies of a real 2-monster encounter carry Weak(1) after turn 1 setup. This is the same mechanism and same closing fix as relic/bag_of_marbles G1 (matched per binding rule 3 when this guard was opened); it is not re-derived here, only re-verified against today's code, which this record had not been since 2026-07-28.

CLOSED, RE-VERIFIED 2026-07-30: red_mask.py:23 still iterates `living_enemies()` rather than the now-available `hittable_enemies()` (relics/base.py:440-451 -- both methods exist today, this relic simply still calls the broader one), but the observable divergence this guard named is gone: `PowerCmd.apply` now carries the `can_receive_powers` backstop this guard's own text said was missing ('PowerCmd.apply does not apply it either ... the missing CanReceivePowers backstop') -- cmds.py:540 and :590 read `if not can_receive_powers(hooks, target): return`, and cmds.py:533's comment dates the fix: 'Round 6 wired the ShouldAllowHitting half'. So an alive-but-unhittable enemy passed to `PowerCmd.apply(WeakPower)` now no-ops regardless of which enemy list the caller built, because the guard lives one layer downstream of the list. EXECUTED (`.superpowers/sdd/unlabelled/probes/relic-6-checks.py::probe_red_mask_slot_and_hittable`): with `should_allow_hitting` forced False for one target, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, target, WeakPower, 1, applier=player)` leaves `target.powers.get('weak')` as `None` -- the same result C#'s `HittableEnemies` pre-filter produces, reached through the backstop instead of the enumeration. Same mechanism and same closing fix as relic/bag_of_marbles G2 (matched per binding rule 3 when opened); the dormancy reasoning this guard gave (the only should_allow_hitting implementer needs a mid-revival state that cannot exist on turn 1) is now moot rather than merely unreached, since the divergence itself is gone.

The participants check restricts a both-sides hook to the owner's own side turn; the sim's on_player_turn_started fires for the player only, so it is structurally satisfied. `self.turn <= 1` (red_mask.py:20) matches `TurnNumber <= 1` with the executed turn numbering (`py audit/tools/relic_probes.py turn-order` prints turn=1 for the first player turn). Note the source uses `<= 1` where relic/radiant_pearl in the same batch uses `== 1`; both partition identically because the counter starts at 1.

guards.what: N2: the multi-target `PowerCmd.Apply<WeakPower>(ctx, combatState.HittableEnemies, ...)` overload (RedMask.cs:28) vs the sim's per-enemy loop
guards.rationale: Both iterate the enemy list in index order and apply the same amount with the same applier (Owner.Creature / `applier=player`); the sim's loop makes the order explicit. The enemy SET is G2's subject, not this entry's. Same disposition as relic/bag_of_marbles N2.

guards.what: N3: WeakPower lands on ENEMIES, so PowerCmd.apply's player-side SkipNextDurationTick arm does not apply
guards.rationale: cmds.py:331-332 sets skip_next_tick only when `target.side == 'player'`, mirroring PowerCmd.Apply's `if (target.Side == CombatSide.Player && power.Type == PowerType.Debuff)` (PowerCmd.cs:144-147). Red Mask debuffs enemies, so the Weak ticks down at the end of the enemy side on both codebases and the relic's 1 Weak covers exactly the first enemy turn. Checked deliberately: had the sim applied the skip to enemies too, the relic would silently last a round longer. NOTE per binding rule 7: cmds.py and PowerCmd.cs are not hashed by this record.
